display.title: Episode 405: The Great Surprise (Parshas Toldos)
display.summary_short: Yaakov and Esav inside each of us, a first-grade class's Shema, and the story of a poor sand-seller whose stolen horse comes home pulling a treasure.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week of Parshas Toldos 5750. Uncle Yossi contrasts Yaakov, who sat in the tents learning Torah, with Esav, who went looking for trouble. Each of us has a little Yaakov, the yetzer tov, and a little Esav, the yetzer hara. Like a seesaw, every mitzvah makes the Yaakov stronger and the Esav weaker; if we ignore the yetzer hara and answer it with a mitzvah, it gives up, and that is how one becomes a tzaddik. When Moshiach comes, evil will vanish altogether. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park recites the Shema with their teacher, and everyone gives tzedakah. The story: Rabbi Yitzchak, a poor, learned man, sells sand from the forest and still gives tzedakah. When a thief steals his horse and wagon, the family says Tehillim and trusts that whatever Hashem does is good. In the forest the thief finds a buried treasure, but the cave collapses on him, and the hungry horse trots home with the treasure on the wagon. The show closes with the mailbox, a sponsor message, a call to join a Shabbos afternoon group, and candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Make your inner Yaakov stronger with every mitzvah and ignore the yetzer hara; trust that whatever Hashem does is good.
